headline: High risk of shared-repo write conflicts and medium risk of prompt/data leakage when Aider and open-webui are paired via files, git, or MCP.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and edits git-tracked files and can execute shell commands, while open-webui can ingest files, documents, and MCP/tool outputs. If content from open-webui is copied into the shared repo or fed through MCP, Aider may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pair has a plausible bridge, though not a guaranteed default one.
conditions: IF open-webui content is written into the shared repository or passed through MCP/tool output to Aider, injection becomes plausible.
IF Aider is configured to act on file contents as trusted instructions, malicious text can steer edits.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted web/chat content into the repo.
Require manual review before Aider applies changes from open-webui outputs.
Use separate workspaces for chat artifacts and source code.
Add a provenance tag or prefix to any content copied between tools.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction-stripping at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history, and open-webui stores prompts, documents, files, notes, and API keys. If they share a workspace or mounted volume, sensitive code or secrets can flow from Aider into open-webui's persistent data surfaces or analytics. The profiles show a real shared-file pathway, but not an unavoidable exfiltration path.
conditions: IF both agents mount the same directory or repo, files can be exposed across the pair.
IF open-webui indexes or persists copied files, source code or git history may be retained beyond the Aider session.
mitigations: Keep open-webui and Aider on separate volumes.
Do not mount the git repo into open-webui.
Restrict open-webui uploads to non-sensitive test data.
Purge open-webui artifacts after each session.
requires-engineering: enforce per-tool access controls on shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and broad network egress; open-webui can run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP/OpenAPI tools with broad network egress. Both can mutate shared resources, and Aider explicitly shares state via a git repo while open-webui supports persistent multi-worker sessions. Concurrent writes can corrupt repo state or overwrite artifacts by default.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git repository or mounted volume, write conflicts are possible.
IF open-webui tools modify files while Aider auto-commits, concurrent state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories to each agent.
Serialize all writes through a single operator-controlled queue.
Pause one agent while the other is committing.
Use branch-per-agent workflows with manual merges.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional commit coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code changes and git commits, while open-webui can present those outputs through chat, documents, or tool calls. If open-webui treats Aider's output as authoritative without verification, mistakes can cascade into downstream actions or persisted memory. The interaction is plausible from the profiles, but not directly evidenced as an automatic action chain.
conditions: IF open-webui forwards Aider-generated text into another tool without validation, errors can propagate.
IF Aider-generated code or claims are stored in open-webui memory, later responses may reuse them uncritically.
mitigations: Require human review before open-webui acts on Aider output.
Mark Aider output as untrusted in open-webui prompts.
Disable automatic memory writes for imported content.
Add a verification step before any downstream tool call.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware trust boundaries.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code, git history, and model provider API keys, while open-webui handles prompts, documents, files, persistent memory, analytics, and API keys. Both are open-source, but open-webui's persistent storage and analytics create a retention/compliance mismatch risk if the same regulated data is routed through both. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into open-webui and then copied into Aider-managed code or git history, retention obligations may diverge.
IF open-webui persistence is enabled for sensitive prompts or files, deletion/export workflows may not match Aider's git history retention.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either tool.
Disable or minimize open-webui persistence for sensitive projects.
Keep secrets out of git-tracked files.
Document retention and deletion procedures for both tools.
requires-engineering: align data-retention and export workflows across the pair.
